plate_initial:
Use case: product-mockup. Create one square premium photorealistic equipment-category photograph for Strength Ledger's PLATE-LOADED machine picker. One unbranded commercial plate-loaded seated chest-press machine, no athlete, no room clutter. The photograph must communicate machine-mounted Olympic weight plates immediately at an 88px square mobile thumbnail.

Scene: seamless near-black OLED studio, subtly textured black rubber floor, dark graphite powder-coated steel frame and black stitched upholstery. Broad neutral-white studio key reveals the mechanics, crisp realistic silver rim highlights on the plates and loading sleeves, restrained violet edge lighting from rear-right with a very faint magenta edge, black background. Premium actual equipment catalog photography, not sci-fi or an illustration.

Camera: tasteful front-left three-quarter view at roughly seated chest height, normal 55mm lens character, one coherent physical perspective. Whole grounded machine fully inside square frame with 7–9% margins, large occupancy. Upright black back pad and smaller horizontal seat in the center, two independently pivoting press arms, real connected pivot brackets, rubber handles in front of the backrest. Both arms have solid horizontal cylindrical loading horns on their outer sides. Mount TWO large round Olympic-style steel weight plates on EACH horn, their round faces and thickness plainly visible. The closer loaded horn and its two plates should be prominent in the central-right area, not at the extreme edge. Plates must visibly slide onto and surround the horn at their center bores; a short polished horn end visibly protrudes beyond each mounted pair. Far-side mounted plates also visible. Circular plates remain circular in physical space, properly foreshortened by the same camera. Unmarked dark brushed steel plate faces with gently bright brushed-metal rims; no stamped letters or weight numbers. A plausible welded wide H-base supports the seat upright and two pivot towers, with believable bolted joints and rubber feet. Frame supports, lever arms, handles and upholstery must not intersect or melt together.

The defining cue is substantial physical discs mounted on machine working loading horns. No weight stack, no selector pin, no cable crossover, no barbell, no rack, no loose plates on floor, no person. No manufacturer logos, labels, typography, numbers, watermarks, symbols or graphic overlays. One single photograph, not a collage. Maintain sharp mechanical detail and readable mounted plates against the graphite machine at tiny picker size.

selector_closeup:
Use case: product-mockup / macro equipment-detail photography.
Create the SELECTORIZED equipment-category asset as a TIGHT CLOSE-UP of a rectangular weight stack and its inserted selector pin. The owner explicitly wants the stack and pin detail, NOT a full machine. The input is ONLY the Strength Ledger material/lighting reference: near-black background, graphite commercial-machine steel, neutral metallic edge highlights, faint violet accent and realistic premium equipment photography. Do not reproduce any round plates, loading horns, seat or full machine from the reference.

A square close-up fills the image with an exposed weight stack: about twelve perfectly aligned rectangular dark gunmetal steel slabs stacked flat against one another, their horizontal seams crisp and their straight edges/individual thicknesses obvious. Camera is close, at the middle of the stack, from a slightly front-right three-quarter angle so we see the broad fronts and a little of their right-side depth. The stack itself occupies roughly 65 percent of the square's width and 80 percent of its height. Two polished vertical guide rods run straight through matching guide holes near the left and right sides of every slab, into the top plate; partial graphite tower frame behind them establishes real machine context. All blocks share one common geometry and perspective, no warped or offset plates.

A single centered vertical column of clean circular selector holes appears in the front faces. ONE selector pin is actually inserted into ONE central slab's selector hole, not suspended in air. Its short steel shaft enters that hole, with a compact round violet polymer pull handle close to the slab front, angled correctly with the face. The handle should be large and clear enough to read as the selector control at a small mobile tile size but remain realistic (roughly 4 cm across, less than one fifth of stack width). A black coiled retention tether connects the pin handle to a nearby fixed frame anchor. Make this inserted pin the sharply focused central feature, alongside the horizontal stack pattern. Other selector holes are empty. The slabs rest together; no floating lifted weights. Subtle realistic metal wear and polished guide rods, smooth manufactured corners, believable apertures and fit.

Controlled neutral studio light reveals ALL the stack seams and the selector pin. Rich near-black surround, graphite mechanism, very restrained violet rim on adjacent frame and a tiny restrained magenta glint if natural. Deep premium material rendering with sharp mechanical edges; no futuristic light strips. Close equipment detail only: no full machine, no upholstery, no wide gym scene, no athlete, no weight discs, no loading sleeve, no barbell, no cable station scene. Natural cropped continuation of the guide rods/frame may leave the image, but the complete slab widths and central pin stay safely inside the square with breathing room.

No numbers, printed weight markings, letters, logos, labels, icons, manufacturer branding, watermarks or text anywhere. One coherent close-up photograph, no diagram, collage or inset. At 80px the immediate read must be rectangular stacked weights with a visible selector-pin handle.
